newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU approves Boeing merger in principle.
newsitem.headline: EU approves Boeing merger in principle.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday gave its preliminary approval to a planned $15 billion merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas.
"There was a broad agreement (within the Commission). The remedies the Commission was striving for have largely been supplied," Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert told a news conference.
Van Miert said Boeing had accepted the Commission's position against the long-term exclusive airplane supply contracts which the U.S. giant had agreed with three U.S. airlines.

He also said Boeing and the Commission had agreed on other key sticking points in the talks between the two sides, with the U.S. firm undertaking not to abuse its dominant position in the global airplane market to influence the aircraft supplies sector.

The Commissioner confirmed that the EU's 20-seat executive would hand down its final formal decision on the merger next week after a review by EU national antitrust experts, adding that he was confident a large majority of these would back the Commission.
